Speech by Governor Lee on Treasury market liquidity

Published 2026-10-06 06:30 UTC

Federal Reserve Governor Jordan Lee spoke on Tuesday about liquidity in the market for U.S. Treasury securities, the deepest and most important government bond market in the world. The governor discussed recent episodes of stress and several possible reforms intended to make the market more resilient.

Governor Lee noted that Treasury market functioning has deteriorated several times in recent years, most notably in March 2020, when even the most liquid securities became difficult to trade. More recently, sharp moves in yields during the spring of this year briefly widened bid-ask spreads and reduced market depth, though conditions normalized within days.

The governor said the size of the Treasury market has grown much faster than the balance sheets of the dealers who traditionally stand ready to buy and sell securities. When many investors want to sell at the same time, dealers may lack the capacity to absorb those sales, which can amplify price swings.

Lee discussed several reforms under consideration. Expanding central clearing of Treasury trades could allow dealers to net offsetting positions and free up balance sheet capacity. Improving data collection on trading activity would help authorities monitor risks. Adjustments to how leverage requirements treat Treasury holdings could also give banks more room to intermediate during periods of stress.

The governor emphasized that the Federal Reserve's standing repo facility provides a backstop for funding markets and that its design is being reviewed to make it more effective. Lee said that reforms should be evaluated together, because changes in one area can affect incentives in others.

Governor Lee concluded that a resilient Treasury market is essential for the transmission of monetary policy and for financial stability, and that the public and private sectors share responsibility for strengthening it. The views expressed are the governor's own and not necessarily those of the Board.
